plan.english: The ram saw the cook, and he trembled in fear.
The sheep followed the ram. He did not look at her.
The master drove the flock to me, and I followed him.
The cook set the fire and cooked the grain.
The queen sat down, and he stood up.
I was thirsty, and I drank.
I put honey on the grain, and I licked it.
Ram, do not eat the wheat! He has seen you.
I did not plough the field, and it did not grow.
I was ploughing with the plough, and the wheat grew.
I crushed the wheat, and I cooked it.
The door said to the fire, "Do not burn me!"
Whoever does not plough does not eat the grain.
I was boiling the grain, and it was steaming.
The queen clothed me, and I went.
I was plaiting, and I was humming.
The other field was bigger than this field, and we ploughed it.
You are hungry. I am satisfied.
He sat down on the rock and was looking at me.
The wheat was bending, and we harvested it.
The sheep was swelling with milk, and I milked her.
The harvest was productive, and it satisfied me.
The blaze devoured the door, and we ran.
He gave me a measure of grain.
He went to the stream and drank.
The plough said to the rock, "You are growing."
The fire burned the cook. The rock did not burn.
The stream was shining, and we drank.
The blood was red, and I trembled.
The back was wet, and I dried it.
The blood covered his head, and he did not see me.
The heat melted the honey, and I licked it.
The plough hit the rock, and it broke.
It was getting dark, and the flock lay down.
He crept to me and sat down.
He swam in the stream, and the stream carried him.
I lifted the plough, and I sweated.
She took the wool and carried it.
He snatched the blood, and I ran.
I laid the wool on the rock, and the heat dried it.
He released the flock, and it ran to me.
He poured the honey on the grain, and it shone.
He roared and made them tremble.
The praiser recited, and we listened.
He followed the blood, and he found the wool.
They were competing, and I was watching them.
He overcame the blaze, and he sat down.
The grain nourishes me, and the honey nourishes you.
The door protects us, and the fire guards us.
The grandson is gone, and I am seeking him.
I am afraid of the blaze, and I am running.
I have reached the stream. Now I am drinking.
We are alert, and we are listening to you.
He knows me, and he is mindful of the harvest.
He belched, and we trembled.
He farted, and a blaze appeared.
He arrived and saw her. She trembled in fear.
She hid, and he sought her. He did not recognize her.
I heard a groan, and I ran.
His back was wet, and his head was red.
The head was broken, and the heat was red.
She was weaving, and he was plaiting.
I was weaving, and you were twisting.
She was knitting, and he was winding.
We were walking, and we were humming.
He was lying down and sweating, and he was thirsty.
The other one looked at him, and he trembled in fear.
He cut off the wool, and she twisted it.
He was splitting it, and I was cutting it off.
I was straightening it, and you were lifting it.
She was smearing it, and he was drying it.
It was getting dark, and we sat down.
He urinated, and she did not look at him.
Who is standing? I am standing.
What are you seeking? I am seeking honey.
What did you see? I saw a blaze.
Are you listening to me? I am listening to you.
What is this? It is wool.
Are you thirsty? I am thirsty. Drink from the stream!
What are you afraid of? I am afraid of the blaze.
Who is hungry? I am hungry. Eat the wheat!
Who knows this? I know it.
Do you recognize me? I recognize you.
Give me the wool! I am giving it to you.
Come to me! I am coming.
Follow me! I am following you.
Lead us! I am leading you.
Do not kill me! I am not killing you.
Protect us! We are protecting you.
Hide me! I am hiding you.
Carry it! I am carrying it.
Haul it! I am hauling it.
Take it! I am taking it.
Seize him! I am seizing him.
Who pushed me? He pushed you.
What is red? The head is red.
Is the master wet? He is wet.
Let us go to him! Let us drink.
Let us sit down, and let us eat.
Let us cook the wheat! Let us eat it.
Let us weave! You twist, and I weave.
Knead the grain! I am kneading it.
Who is milking? I am milking.
Who ploughed? You ploughed, and I harvested.
What did he say? He said, "Go!"
Is the grain boiling? It is boiling.
Is it burning? It is burning.
What are you cooking? I am cooking the sheep.
Show me the head! I am showing it to you.
Point it out! I am pointing it out.
Do you want to see it? I want to see it.
What are you thinking? I am thinking about it.
Are you confident? I am confident.
Are you awake? I am alert.
Who went? He went to you.
Who arrived? I arrived.
Are you leaving? I am leaving you.
Did you not see me? I did not see you.
May you be satisfied and not thirsty.
Stand up! I stood up.
Let him come! Let him sit down.
Give him the grain! He gives it to you.
What did you put down? I put down the rock.
Who is carrying the plough around? We are carrying it around.
Are you transporting it? We are transporting it.
Who is reciting? The praiser is reciting.
Which one is coming? This one is coming.
Is he bigger than you? I am bigger.
What is trembling? I am trembling.
Who is sweating? We are sweating.
Who is breathing? Whoever lives is breathing.
Who is playing? We are playing.
Is he speaking? He is speaking to you.
Who is walking? We are walking.
Who jumped? He jumped, and I ran.
Are you swimming? I am swimming.
Who is creeping up? I am creeping.
Who is at work? I am creating heat.
Who arranged the fire? I arranged it.
What shall we sacrifice? Let us sacrifice honey.
Join us! We joined you.
Who is driving? I am driving.
Are you cutting it? I am cutting it off.
Who split it? I split it.
Is he able? He is able.
Are you upset? I am afraid.
Who is burning? I am burning.
Who is heating it? I am heating it.
Did you cook it? I cooked it.
Are you listening to it? Listen!
The master begot the giver, and the giver begot the praiser.
The queen bore a grandson, and she nourished him.
The giver led the queen, and she bore him a grandson.
The giver's grandson has been born, and he lives.
The giver's grandson became a cook, and he cooked the grain.
We are the master's grandsons, and we live.
Whoever is born lives.
I was born, and you are grown.
He begot me, and I begot you.
She nourished me, and I nourished him.
He led her, and she followed him.
May you live, and may you grow.
The giver was greater than the cook, and the cook was greater than I.
He led me, and I led you.
He lives, and I live, and you live.
He arrived and settled us.
You lived, and you arrived, and you settled us.
The praiser's mind was greater than I.
They were born, and they grew.
He killed him, and we settled.
May we live, and may we be satisfied.
Who stands steady? He stands steady.
Who settled us? He settled us.
He has been born, and he is grown, and he lives.
Who is grown? You are grown.
Whoever settles us nourishes us.
May he be grown, and may he live.
She has been born, and she is grown.
Who came to be? I came to be.
He stands steady, and he is productive.
Whoever kills a ram shall give a sheep.
Whoever seizes the flock shall release it.
Whoever hides the plough shall give a measure.
Whoever burns the field shall give a measure.
Whoever does not guard the fire shall give a vow.
Do not kill the sheep! Do not hide her!
Do not push the ram! Do not seize him!
Let him guard the door, and let him protect the fire.
Do not strike him on the head!
Whoever gives a vow shall hear it.
Whoever snatches it shall give it back to me.
Whoever kills him, let me kill him.
Do not take the blood! Do not snatch it!
Let him sit down, and let him drink.
Whoever harvests shall give a measure of the harvest.
Do not drive the flock into the field!
Whoever sees blood shall not hide it.
Do not carry the fire in the heat!
Give him a vow!
Whoever leaves us shall not eat.
Whoever says a falsehood shall give a measure.
Do not speak a falsehood! Do not say it!
Whoever knows this, let him say it.
Whoever hears this shall know it.
Whoever works shall eat the harvest.
Whoever is hungry shall eat, and whoever is thirsty shall drink.
Clothe him! Seat him!
Give him a measure!
Do not leave him!
Whoever kills shall be killed.
Whoever lifts it shall carry it.
Whoever recognizes it shall show it to me.
Let him who knows point it out.
Whoever is able shall lift it.
Whoever is awake shall guard it.
Whoever trembles shall not speak.
Do not look at it! Do not listen to it!
Whoever arrives shall sit down, and whoever leaves shall stand up.
Whoever follows me shall eat.
Do not haul it! Do not lift it!
O queen, hear us, and protect us!
O fire, you are shining, and you protect us.
O master, you are shining, and you give us the harvest.
O praiser, recite! We shall listen.
May the field be productive, and may the flock grow.
May the harvest be productive, and may we eat.
May the fire shine, and may it warm the door.
We recite for you, and you listen to us.
You are productive, and you are shining.
Shine, O fire, and warm us!
May the heat not kill us!
May the door protect us, and may the fire guard us.
You see us, and you recognize us.
Come, O master, and sit down!
Stand up, O praiser, and recite!
The queen shines, and we see her.
You shine, and you are red.
May the sheep and the ram be satisfied.
We give you a vow, and you listen to it.
We are mindful of you, and we recognize you.
Let us speak, and let us give.
May we see you, and may you hear us.
We are standing, and we are listening to you.
You know, and you see.
O mind, be awake, and know!
Hear us! Come to us!
May we be satisfied, and may we not be hungry.
You lift us up, and you carry us.
You are shining, and we are trembling.
May we see the shining one!
